title: Domain & Range, Composite, Inverse
videoTitle: Domain & Range, Composite, Inverse [IB Math AI HL]
intro: After this lesson you can evaluate a function, state its domain and range, build the composites $f\circ g$ and $g\circ f$, and find an inverse function, restricting the domain first when the function is not one-to-one.

moments.title: Three ways to write a function
moments.text: $f(x)=x^2-2$, $f: x\mapsto x^2-2$ and $y=x^2-2$ all describe the same rule. Use whichever your textbook uses.

moments.title: Evaluate by substitution
moments.text: $f(3)=7$, $g(-2)=1$ and $h(24)=5$. Find the function, then substitute the input for $x$.

moments.title: Domain and range
moments.text: The domain is the set of possible inputs ($x$ values). The range is the set of possible outputs ($y$ values).

moments.title: Domain and range of a quadratic
moments.text: $f(x)=x^2-2$ goes left and right forever, so $x\in\mathbb{R}$. It bottoms out at $-2$, so $y\ge-2$.

moments.title: A straight line
moments.text: $g(x)=x+3$ goes on forever in every direction, so both domain and range are all real numbers.

moments.title: A square root function
moments.text: $h(x)=\sqrt{x+1}$ starts at $x=-1$ and only gives non-negative outputs: domain $x\ge-1$, range $y\ge0$.

moments.title: A composite is a function of a function
moments.text: In $f\circ g$, the output of $g$ becomes the input of $f$.

moments.title: Find $f\circ g$
moments.text: Write $f$, and where it has $x$, put in $g(x)=x+3$. The result is $(x+3)^2-2$.

moments.title: Find $g\circ f$
moments.text: Start with $g$ and put $f(x)$ where $x$ was: $x^2-2+3=x^2+1$. A different order gives a different function.

moments.title: Inverse functions and their notation
moments.text: The inverse of $f$ is written $f^{-1}$. Start from $y=f(x)$.

moments.title: Swap $x$ and $y$, then solve for $y$
moments.text: The first step is always to swap $x$ and $y$. Then use algebra to make $y$ the subject.

moments.title: The inverse of $h$
moments.text: From $y=\sqrt{x+1}$: swap, square both sides, subtract 1. $h^{-1}(x)=x^2-1$.

moments.title: The inverse is a reflection
moments.text: The graph of $f^{-1}$ is the graph of $f$ reflected in the line $y=x$.

corrections.title: The video only inverts a quadratic and a square root
corrections.text: The exam often asks for the inverse of rational, exponential, or logarithmic functions too. The method is the same.
corrections.write: Switch $x$ and $y$, then solve for $y$. Use $\ln$ to undo $\mathrm{e}^{y}$ and $\mathrm{e}$ to undo $\ln y$. For $y=4+\dfrac{6}{x-1}$ the inverse is $1+\dfrac{6}{x-4}$.

corrections.title: The video inverts $x^2-2$ without restricting the domain
corrections.text: It swaps and solves to get $\sqrt{x+2}$, but $f(x)=x^2-2$ on all real numbers is not one-to-one, so it has no inverse there.
corrections.write: $f(x)=x^2-2$ is not one-to-one on $\mathbb{R}$, so restrict it first, for example to $x\ge0$. In the exam the function usually comes with a domain that already makes it one-to-one.

corrections.title: The video does not give the domain or range of an inverse
corrections.text: It finds $h^{-1}(x)=x^2-1$ but does not say where that function is defined or what its range is.
corrections.write: The domain of $h^{-1}$ is the range of $h$ ($x\ge0$) and its range is the domain of $h$ ($y\ge-1$). Many questions say the domain is not required, but others ask you to write it down.

sections.title: Does the function have an inverse?

cards.name: Test
cards.text: Does every output come from only one input? A horizontal line crosses the graph at most once.

cards.name: Restrict
cards.text: If not, keep one side of the turning point so the function is one-to-one.

cards.name: Swap and solve
cards.text: Write $y=f(x)$, swap $x$ and $y$, then solve for $y$.

cards.name: Domains swap
cards.text: The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$. The range of $f^{-1}$ is the domain of $f$.

cells: None until the domain is restricted

notes.label: Wording check.
notes.text: The video finds $f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x+2}$ for $f(x)=x^2-2$ without restricting the domain first. A function needs to be one-to-one to have an inverse. Exam questions usually give a domain that already works, and often say the domain of the inverse is not required. If you are given a function like this one, state a restriction such as $x\ge0$ before you swap.

sections.title: Composite and inverse functions: the method
sections.intro: A composite function feeds the output of one function into another. An inverse undoes a function. Both come from substitution and rearranging.
steps: To find $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$, write $f$, then replace every $x$ in it with the whole expression for $g(x)$.
Simplify if the question asks. Check the order: $f\circ g$ and $g\circ f$ are usually different functions.
To find $f^{-1}$, first check that $f$ is one-to-one on its domain. If it is not, restrict the domain.
Write $y=f(x)$, swap $x$ and $y$, then solve for $y$. That $y$ is $f^{-1}(x)$.
State the domain of $f^{-1}$. It is the range of $f$.

parts.label: Composite: f then g
parts.text: With $f(x)=x^2-2$ and $g(x)=x+3$, replace the $x$ in $f$ with $x+3$. Expanded, $(f\circ g)(x)=x^2+6x+7$.

parts.label: Composite: g then f
parts.text: Start with $g$ and replace its $x$ with $x^2-2$: $(g\circ f)(x)=(x^2-2)+3=x^2+1$. A different order gives a different function.

parts.label: Inverse, with the restriction
parts.text: For $f(x)=x^2-2$ with $x\ge0$: write $y=x^2-2$, swap to $x=y^2-2$, so $y^2=x+2$ and $y=\sqrt{x+2}$ (positive root, because $y\ge0$). The domain is $x\ge-2$.

sections.title: Inverse and reflection explorer
sections.intro: Drag the horizontal line across the graph to test whether $f$ is one-to-one. Then show the inverse and see that it is the reflection of $f$ in the line $y=x$. The grid has the same scale on both axes, like the calculator after Zoom Square.

stories.quad: The video's first function, $f(x)=x^2-2$. Put the line at $y=1$: it crosses twice, so two inputs give one output. Show the inverse and check it with the vertical line. Then keep only the right side of the vertex.
stories.sqrt: The video's third function, $h(x)=\sqrt{x+1}$, is already one-to-one on its domain $x\ge-1$. Its inverse is $h^{-1}(x)=x^2-1$ for $x\ge0$. Notice that the inverse stops at $x=0$, the lowest output of $h$.
stories.shift: $p(x)=(x-1)^2+4$ has its vertex at $(1,4)$. Raise the line above 4 and it crosses twice. Keep $x\ge1$ and the inverse is $1+\sqrt{x-4}$.
stories.line: $g(x)=x+3$ is one-to-one everywhere. Its inverse is $x-3$, the reflection of the line in $y=x$. The mirror point swaps the coordinates.

sections.title: What the exam asks and where the marks go
asks: Find an expression for $f^{-1}(x)$ from a formula, usually on Paper 1. The question often says the domain is not required. The function is often rational, exponential, or logarithmic, not only a quadratic.
Find the range of $f$ from a given domain, using the end values and any asymptote. The range of $f^{-1}$ is then the domain of $f$.
Find an inverse value such as $f^{-1}(10)$ in a context, then say what it means in a sentence.
Sketch $f^{-1}$ by reflecting the graph of $f$ in the line $y=x$, or complete a table of inverse values by swapping inputs and outputs.
Solve $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)$ by sketching both graphs and finding the intersection.
Write $f\circ g$ and $g\circ f$ in a context, say which order matches the situation, and compare the results.

marks.label: Finding an inverse
marks.text: Usually 3 marks: (M1) for isolating $x$ or $y$, M1 for switching $x$ and $y$ (it can be seen anywhere), and A1 for the expression.

marks.label: The range
marks.text: A1 for both end values and A1 for a correct interval. Using a strict inequality where the end value is included, or the other way round, loses a mark.

marks.label: Range of the inverse
marks.text: The range of $f^{-1}$ is the domain of $f$, with the same kind of inequality. It is usually 1 or 2 marks, and some markschemes say not to follow through an earlier error here.

marks.label: An inverse value in context
marks.text: M1 for writing $f(x)=$ the value (a sketch showing the intersection also earns it), A1 for the value, and A1 for a sentence in context. A sentence that states the converse is condoned.

marks.label: Comparing composites
marks.text: M1 for discussing the order in which the steps happen, and R1 for a reason or the numbers that show it. The A1 conclusion is not awarded without the R1.

sections.gdc: The GDC is allowed on every paper. To find $f^{-1}(a)$ without algebra, graph $f$ and the line $y=a$ and find the intersection. To solve $f(x)=f^{-1}(x)$, graph both and find where they meet. A sketch that shows the intersection earns the method mark.

traps.title: The order of a composite
traps.better: $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$, so $g$ acts first and then $f$. In practice, replace the $x$ in $f$ with $g(x)$.

traps.title: An inverse needs a one-to-one function
traps.better: $f(x)=x^2-2$ is not one-to-one on $\mathbb{R}$, so give it a restricted domain first, such as $x\ge0$. If the question already gives a domain, use that one.

traps.title: The inverse is not a reciprocal
traps.better: $f^{-1}$ is the inverse function, found by switching $x$ and $y$. The reciprocal $\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$ is a different function.

traps.title: Strict or not strict
traps.better: Domain: $x\ge-1$, because $h(-1)=\sqrt{0}=0$ is defined. Range: $y\ge0$. The wrong kind of inequality loses an A mark.

traps.title: Domain and range swap
traps.better: The range of $h^{-1}$ is the domain of $h$: $y\ge-1$. The domain of $h^{-1}$ is the range of $h$: $x\ge0$.

traps.title: Give 3 significant figures
traps.better: $x=5.37$, to 3 significant figures. Keep the full calculator value until the last step.

sections.title: Try an exam-style question
sections.prompt: A function is defined by $f(x)=4+\dfrac{6}{x-1}$ for $x>1$.

parts.text: (b) Find an expression for $f^{-1}(x)$. The domain is not required.
(c) Write down the domain and the range of $f^{-1}$.

lines.text: recognizes that $\dfrac{6}{x-1}>0$ for $x>1$, or the horizontal asymptote $y=4$
an attempt to isolate $x$ (or $y$ if switched): $x-1=\dfrac{6}{y-4}$
the domain of $f^{-1}$ is $x>4$, the range of $f$
the range of $f^{-1}$ is $f^{-1}(x)>1$, the domain of $f$
a sketch of $f$ and $f^{-1}$ showing the intersection, or the equation $f(x)=x$

sections.note: Work it on paper first. The GDC is allowed: graph $f$, $f^{-1}$ and $y=x$ to check part (d).

footer: Built from the video's auto-generated captions. Practice questions are newly written.

flags.text: The video inverts f(x)=x^2-2 on all real numbers and gives sqrt(x+2) without saying f must be one-to-one first. The page adds the domain restriction (the syllabus lists it for AHL 2.7) and shows it in the decision table and a wording trap.
The video does not state the domain of an inverse function. The page adds that the domain of the inverse is the range of the original (rows and traps for f and h).

The exam section uses statistics from the IB question bank (HL applications and interpretation questions, 2021 to 2025) and a reading of the markschemes for this topic; no question text or question numbers are shown. The exam-style question and its markscheme are newly written. Syllabus codes SL 2.2 and AHL 2.7. The video covers function notation, domain and range (SL 2.2) as well as composite and inverse functions (AHL 2.7). The identity (f o f^-1)(x)=x and the rows for g, p, and the x<=0 branch of f are not in the video; they come from the syllabus guidance.

Captions at about 0:45 ('a little pole in here as X with a little arrow') mean the maps-to notation f: x -> x^2-2, and at 2:10 ('my is positive one') means 'my output is 1'. Notation was rebuilt from context.
Every value on the page was computed and checked with sympy. Domain and range statements and the inverse domains were worked out from the function definitions, not read off graphs.
No GDC section: no emulator captures exist yet for this topic. The video suggests graphing h on a calculator (about 6:15), which would suit a later GDC section.
Decision rows for g, p and the x<=0 branch have no video link because the video does not cover them.
